source: Web search for 2026 replications of CompressARC (gap 1)
finding: A targeted search found no 2026 paper that replicates, reproduces or extends CompressARC. The only hits are the original paper and secondary summaries.
numbers: 0 replication papers found in 2 searches. ARC Prize 2025 lists it as a 3rd-place paper award.
limits: Absence of evidence from a search engine, not proof. Citation lists were not checked in Semantic Scholar or OpenAlex (HTTP 429 rate limits) or arXiv API (429).
agent_relevance: Gap 1 stays open. Treat the 20% as one team's number.

source: Liao and Gu (2025) ARC-AGI Without Pretraining, Appendix O and code repository (gap 1)
finding: Code is public under MIT licence. The README gives one run command per task on one RTX 4070 and up to 20 minutes per task. It gives no headline accuracy, no seed information and no ARC-AGI-2 support.
numbers: Example log: 1500 steps in 12:22 (about 2.01 it/s). list_solved_puzzles.py counts solved puzzles at 2 guesses and up to 4000 guesses. 3 open issues (content not read).
limits: README publishes no expected numbers, so a third party cannot check a reproduction against it. Seed handling not described.
agent_relevance: We can run the solver as a side tool. A seed-variance run is still ours to do.

source: Liao and Gu (2025) ARC-AGI Without Pretraining, Section 5.2.1 and Appendix K (gaps 2, 9)
finding: The paper reports no ablation of its own components. The only control is the U-Net baseline. Appendix K lists untested ideas: weight sharing, a KL floor, weight-cost regularisation. No reconstruction-only control with the same equivariant network is reported.
numbers: U-Net 2.5% on train without augmentation, 1% with. No seed variance reported. K.3: authors have never seen a collapsed tensor recover. K.4: leaving out the weight cost is called somewhat reckless.
limits: Appendix K is a wish list, not results. Read via HTML conversion; in one fetch the appendix H failure list was cut off.
agent_relevance: Gaps 2 and 9 stay open. The claim that compression itself causes the gain is untested.

source: Liao and Gu (2025) ARC-AGI Without Pretraining, Sections 5 and 6 (gap 8)
finding: Cost is about 20 minutes per puzzle for 2000 steps on one RTX 4070. Runtime scales with pixel count. Learning happens only on the target puzzle.
numbers: About 20 min per puzzle; 400 puzzles about 130-138 h (earlier evidence). Our arithmetic: 20 min / 0.20 solved at pass@2 = about 100 GPU-minutes per solved eval puzzle.
limits: No dollar cost. No same-item cost comparison with TTT or LLMs in the paper.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 partly closed: CompressARC about 100 GPU-min per solve, Kaggle TTT $0.20 per task, LLM refinement $31-60 per task (d05).

finding: CompressARC took 3rd place in the paper awards and is described as an MDL-based zero-pretraining system with about 4% on ARC-AGI-2. The report lists Kaggle ARC-AGI-2 private scores and cost per task for several systems.
numbers: CompressARC: 76K params, 20% ARC-1 eval, about 20 min per puzzle, 4% ARC-AGI-2. Kaggle private ARC-AGI-2: NVARC 24.03% at $0.20 per task, ARChitects 16.53%, MindsAI 12.64%, Lonnie 6.67%, Barbadillo 6.53%. Gemini 3 Pro 31% at $0.81 per task; with Poetiq refinement 54% at $31 per task; Opus 4.5 same harness about $60 per task.
limits: The 4% is a one-line summary with no table or method detail. Frontier rows not labelled semi-private in the text read.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: about 4% on ARC-AGI-2 means the method does not transfer to harder tasks. Gap 8: cost ladder from $0.20 to $60 per task.

source: Rodionov (2026) Do Coding Agents Need Executable World Models, Simplification, and Verification to Solve ARC-AGI-3?
finding: Closest 2026 LLM-agent work to compression at inference time. It tests a simplification prompt (a practical MDL proxy, not a description-length objective) with Codex agents on 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games. Simplification beat its executable-only counterpart in 3 of 4 model settings.
numbers: Mean RHAE, textual / executable / simplification / verification. gpt-5.4 high 34.16/33.54/30.60/39.16; gpt-5.4 xhigh 40.67/44.72/53.10/53.72; gpt-5.5 high 58.85/51.16/58.35/65.64; gpt-5.5 xhigh 72.51/69.70/73.09/74.78. Cost tokens (millions): simplification 127-176 (gpt-5.4), 138-163 (gpt-5.5); textual 63-98.
limits: One run per game per block. Public games only, contamination possible. No simplification-on-textual arm, so the gain cannot be assigned to simplicity. Simplification used about 1.6-2.4x the tokens of textual, so it is not equal-token.
agent_relevance: Gaps 3 and 7 partly: a prompt-level simplicity push can help (-3.0 to +8.4 points over executable) but costs more tokens and is not a measured MDL stopping rule.

source: Rodionov (2026) simplification prompts, schedule and limits
finding: Simplification prompts are sent on a fixed schedule (one light prompt early, then three broader passes, then a planner refactor). They set no numeric complexity target and do not optimise or measure description length.
numbers: Verification used 1.82-3.26x textual tokens and 1.16-1.49x simplification tokens. Median wall-clock 4 h 26 min per playthrough, max 53 h.
limits: Exact prompt text (Section 12.4) not read. Advisory enforcement only.
agent_relevance: Our schema could add a cheap periodic 'replace special cases by a general rule' step; evidence of benefit is weak and unisolated.

source: Habr write-up of the ARC-AGI-3 coding agent (secondary)
finding: A secondary article agrees the simplicity bias is a stand-in for MDL. It repeats the ablation: text-only context beat the executable simulator, verification ranked first, simplification helped in 3 of 4 configurations. The writer argues the benchmark cannot tell brute force from understanding.
limits: Secondary Russian-language blog; opinions are not evidence.
agent_relevance: Warns that action-count scores can hide heavy off-game computation.

finding: With a newer model the verification variant completed all public levels at about 99% human-relative efficiency. The author says this shows public-set saturation only.
numbers: ewma_sv v1.6, gpt-5.6-sol xhigh: RHAE 98.97, 8,347 actions vs human baseline 17,135, cost 90.75M tokens. twma v1.6 xhigh 92.34 at 32.32M tokens.
limits: Exploratory, single runs, model released after the games.
agent_relevance: Do not read these as evidence that compression helps; the model upgrade dominates.

source: Pourcel, Colas, Oudeyer (2025) SOAR: self-improving program synthesis on ARC-AGI
finding: LLM program-synthesis search picks answers by voting weighted by train accuracy, not by program length. This is the LLM-side alternative to CompressARC at test time.
numbers: Single attempt: Claude-4-Sonnet 20.75%, GPT-4.1 8.00%. Sample-6k 5.63-19.75% across five open models; Sample&Refine-6k 14.25-26.25%; SOAR-6k fine-tuned 36.25-45.50%. Ensemble 52% (majority over 5 models, about 30,000 attempts per task); oracle 57.25%. Weight = count + 1000 x train accuracy.
limits: Public ARC-test split. Selection ignores program length. Fine-tuning uses LoRA rank 256, so a closed-API agent cannot copy it. Page read to 100k of 143k characters.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: voting loses 5.25 points to the oracle at 30k samples. Gap 3: no MDL-based selection tested.

source: Cole and Osman (2025) Don't throw the baby out with the bathwater: how and why deep learning for ARC (AIRV)
finding: AIRV (augment, infer, reverse-augment, vote) lifts a fine-tuned LongT5 on private ARC. No study of augmentation voting with a closed-API LLM was found.
numbers: Base zero-shot 5; AIRV only 13; TTFT+AIRV 39 (garbled table, my reading); best 58% on the private ARC set in 2024. AIRV gain up to 260%; TTFT about 300%.
limits: Number of augmentations not stated. Weights are trained. No mention of MDL.
agent_relevance: Gap 5 stays open for closed APIs: stability voting is proven only with local trained models.

finding: A 200M LongT5-based pipeline with LoRA test-time training, 18 augmented views, beam 10 and likelihood scoring over 8 D4 transforms reaches 27% on ARC-AGI-2 semi-private. No mention of compression or MDL in the text read.
numbers: 12.08% and 19.86% earlier stages; 25.00% with traversal augmentation; 27% final. LoRA r=8, 35 epochs, lr 8e-4. Up to 180 candidates. Kaggle limit 4xL4, 12 h for 240 tasks. 2.3M synthetic pretraining tasks.
limits: Page truncated after Section 5.6. Summary table and scoring formula disagree on snake traversal.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: pretrained TTT with likelihood selection gets 27% on ARC-AGI-2 versus about 4% for CompressARC.

source: Talley et al. (2026) Multi-Perspective Transformers in ARC-AGI-2 Challenge
finding: TinyLM with test-time fine-tuning and product of experts. Abstract reports a large train-to-eval gap.
numbers: 96.1% training set, 21.7% evaluation set on ARC-AGI-2.
limits: Abstract only; no ablation of TTT or PoE read.
agent_relevance: More test-time-training evidence on ARC-AGI-2, not compression.

source: Search for LLM proposer plus description-length selection (gaps 3, 7); LLM-PV abstract (arXiv 2510.14331)
finding: No paper was found that uses an LLM as proposer with a description-length criterion to choose answers or to stop. LLM-PV proposes programs with an LLM and selects by held-out validation score. Description length appears only as motivation.
agent_relevance: Gaps 3 and 7: no direct evidence either way. Stay open; a small own experiment is needed.

source: ARC Prize 2025 results and analysis blog (snippet only)
finding: Snippet-level: refinement loops are the 2025 theme; CompressARC listed as a single-puzzle MDL system.
limits: Snippet only; rely on the technical report (d05).

source: Gap 4 search: overlap of CompressARC solved set with LLM or TTT systems
finding: No published comparison of which puzzles CompressARC solves versus an LLM or TTT system. The repo has a per-puzzle solved-list script that would allow the overlap to be computed.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 stays open but is cheap: intersect the released solved list with our scaffold results.

source: Emergent Mind topic page on CompressARC (secondary)
finding: The aggregator page lists no citing follow-ups or reproductions. Its references are the original paper and unrelated compression papers.
